relevance_reason: The paper describes two autosomal dominant nanophthalmos pedigrees with novel TMEM98 mutations, which directly supports the NNO4 entry.

findings.statement: Khorram et al. (2015) studied a Caucasian family of German heritage living in the United States (pedigree 991-F) with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos spanning at least 4 generations. Six of 10 examined members had nanophthalmos, and 3 more were affected by family history report. Affected members had a mean axial eye length of 17.1 +/- 0.31 mm and high hyperopia, with spherical equivalent refractions of +13.0 +/- 0.89 diopters. Unaffected members had +0.71 +/- 0.81 diopters.
quotes: Six of ten examined members of pedigree 991-F were diagnosed with nanophthalmos while an additional three members had nanophthalmos according to the family history report. Mean axial eye lengths were 17.1 mm±0.31 mm for the available patients.
Affected family members also had a high degree of hyperopia with spherical equivalent refractions of +13.0±0.89 diopters (Table 1).
a Caucasian family of German heritage living in the United States

findings.statement: Khorram et al. (2015) described a Pacific Islander family of Micronesian heritage from the Mariana Islands (pedigree 951-N) with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos. Eight of 10 examined members were affected, and 3 more were affected by family history report. Affected members had a mean axial eye length of 17.4 +/- 0.94 mm, compared with 22.7 +/- 0.38 mm in unaffected members, and hyperopia of +3.93 +/- 1.57 diopters. Axial lengths across both families ranged from 15.9 to 18.4 mm.
quotes: Eight of ten examined members of Pacific Islander pedigree 951-N had nanophthalmos and an average axial eye length of 17.4 mm±0.94 mm, while unaffected family members had more normal eye length (22.7±0.38 mm; Table 2).
family members with nanophthalmos also had hyperopia with spherical equivalent refractions of +3.93±1.57 diopters.
The patients with nanophthalmos had abnormally short axial eye lengths, which ranged from 15.9 to 18.4 mm.
findings.population: Pacific Islander, Micronesian heritage, Mariana Islands

findings.statement: Khorram et al. (2015) carried out linkage analysis with 6,020 SNPs. In pedigree 991-F, a 20.2-Mb segment of chromosome 17p12-q12 between SNPs rs530664 and rs16523 cosegregated with nanophthalmos. In pedigree 951-N, an overlapping 19.7-Mb region between rs917541 and rs16523 cosegregated with the disease. The authors noted that this region overlapped the locus previously linked to nanophthalmos in a Chinese pedigree.
quotes: In pedigree 991-F, a 20.2 Mbp segment of chromosome 17p12-q12, bounded by SNPs rs530664 and rs16523, was transmitted with nanophthalmos in all members of the family.
An overlapping 19.7 Mb section of chromosome 17, bounded by SNPs rs917541 and rs16523, was similarly coinherited with nanophthalmos in pedigree 951-N.

findings.statement: Exome sequencing of an affected member of the US pedigree 991-F found 4 nonsynonymous variants in the linked chromosome 17 region. Khorram et al. (2015) reported that only the heterozygous His196Pro missense mutation in TMEM98 cosegregated with nanophthalmos and was predicted to be pathogenic by SIFT, PolyPhen, and BLOSUM62. The mutation affects a highly conserved histidine and was absent from the Exome Variant Server and 1000 Genomes Project databases.
quotes: Of the four variants, only the His196Pro mutation in TMEM98 was coinherited with nanophthalmos, absent from healthy family members, and had pathogenic scores on all three sequence analysis systems (Table 3).
Neither the His196Pro mutation nor the 34 bp deletion was detected in public DNA sequence databases including the Exome Variation Server and the 1000 Genomes Project.

findings.statement: In the Mariana Islands pedigree 951-N, Khorram et al. (2015) used Sanger sequencing to identify a heterozygous 34-bp deletion in TMEM98 (c.694_721delAGAATGAAGACTGGATCGAAGATGCCTCgtaagg) in all 11 affected members tested. The deletion spans the last 28 bp of exon 4 and the first 6 bp of intron 4, eliminates a splice site, and results in premature termination of translation. It was absent from healthy family members and from public databases.
quotes: A novel 34 bp heterozygous deletion was detected in all affected family members that spans the last 28 bp of exon 4 and the first 6 bp of intron 4 (c.694_721delAGAATGAAGACTGGATCGAAGATGCCTCgtaagg).
This TMEM98 deletion eliminates a splice site and results in a premature termination of translation.

relevance_reason: This paper first identified a TMEM98 mutation in a large white family with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos linked to 17p12-q12.

findings.statement: Awadalla et al. (2014) studied a large white family (NNO-SA1) with autosomal dominant nanophthalmos. The family was recruited in South Australia. Nanophthalmos was defined as an axial length less than 20.0 mm and/or a refractive error greater than +7.00. Of 35 available family members, 16 (46%) had nanophthalmos, with a mean refraction of +11.8 D and a mean axial length of 17.6 mm.
quotes: Of the 35 available individuals from family NNO-SA1, 16 participants (46%) had a diagnosis of nanophthalmos, with mean refraction of +11.8 D and mean axial length of 17.6 mm.
Nanophthalmos was defined as an axial length less than 20.0 mm and/or refractive error greater than +7.00.

findings.statement: In family NNO-SA1, Awadalla et al. (2014) ran a genome-wide linkage scan with a 10K SNP array. They found significant linkage on chromosome 17 (17p12-q12) between SNP markers rs2323659 and rs967293, with a maximum location score of 4.1.
quotes: Significant linkage was detected on chromosome 17 between single-nucleotide polymorphism markers rs2323659 and rs967293, with a maximum location score of 4.1.

findings.statement: In affected members of family NNO-SA1, Awadalla et al. (2014) used exome sequencing to identify a heterozygous missense variant, c.577G>C (p.Ala193Pro), in exon 8 of the TMEM98 gene. It was the only novel segregating variant within the linked region. The variant was absent from the Exome Variant Server and from 285 local white controls. The authors concluded that TMEM98 most likely causes the disease in this family.
quotes: Exome sequencing identified a single novel segregating missense variant within the linkage region located in exon 8 of the transmembrane-98 (TMEM98) gene c.577G>C (p.Ala193Pro), which was absent in the Exome Variant Server database and among 285 local white individuals serving as controls.
A novel gene associated with nanophthalmos, TMEM98 most likely represents the cause of the disease in this family.

findings.statement: Using RT-PCR, Awadalla et al. (2014) found that TMEM98 was expressed in all ocular tissues tested, including the sclera and the optic nerve head.
quotes: The TMEM98 gene was expressed in all ocular tissues tested including sclera and optic nerve head.

relevance_reason: Describes a Chinese family with autosomal dominant congenital simple microphthalmia and maps the locus to 17p12-q12, which defines the NNO4 locus.

findings.statement: Hu et al. (2011) studied a Chinese family with autosomal dominant congenital simple microphthalmia.
quotes: To investigate the etiology in a family with autosomal-dominant congenital simple microphthalmia of Chinese origin.

findings.statement: In a Chinese family with autosomal dominant congenital simple microphthalmia, Hu et al. (2011) excluded previously reported microphthalmia loci and performed a genomewide scan with 382 microsatellite markers, then fine mapping. They found the highest linkage at D17S1824 (maximum lod score of 4.97 at theta = 0.00). Haplotype analysis placed the disease gene in a 21.57-cM interval between D17S900 and D17S1872 on chromosome 17p12-q12.
quotes: A whole-genome scan was performed by using 382 microsatellite DNA markers after the exclusion of reported candidates linked to microphthalmia.
The most statistically significant linkage results were obtained at D17S1824 (maximum LOD score, 4.97, at recombination fraction 0.00).
Haplotype analyses supported the location of the disease-causing gene to a 21.57-cM interval between loci D17S900 and D17S1872 of chromosome 17, region p12-q12.

findings.statement: Hu et al. (2011) used PCR and direct sequencing to screen 14 candidate genes in the linked 17p12-q12 region, including CRYBA1 and NCOR1. They also used genomewide SNP genotyping to look for copy number variation. They found no mutation or CNV that accounted for the microphthalmia in the family.
quotes: 14 candidate genes including CRYBA1 and NCOR1 were selected to screen for the mutation by the PCR direct-sequencing method.
However, no mutation or CNV (copy number variation) was identified to be responsible for the microphthalmia phenotype of this pedigree.

relevance_reason: This paper describes the Chinese autosomal dominant simple microphthalmia (nanophthalmos) family. Linkage analysis excluded the known loci, so the paper supports a separate, novel locus.

findings.statement: Yu et al. (2009) described a 5-generation Chinese family with isolated (simple) microphthalmia inherited in an autosomal dominant manner. There were 9 affected members aged 6 to 66 years. All had bilateral hyperopia ranging from +4.50 to +11.50 diopters (mean +8.00) and short axial length of 18.22 to 20.26 mm (mean 19.29 mm). Best corrected visual acuity was less than 0.5 in most eyes, and no family member had any other physical anomaly.
quotes: Nine microphthalmia patients from the ages of 6–66 years (mean: 42.8 years) expressed the same full phenotype as previously reported.
Combined hyperopia ranged from +4.50 to +11.50 diopters (mean: +8.00 diopters). The axial length was from 18.22 mm to 20.26 mm (mean: 19.29 mm), which was shorter than the normal length of 23–24 mm.
All family members did not have any other physical anomalies.

findings.statement: In this family, Yu et al. (2009) reported angle-closure glaucoma or occludable anterior chamber angles in 3 patients, all older than 50 years. The glaucoma was treated by trabeculectomy but kept progressing, and 2 patients eventually developed atrophia bulbi despite repeated surgeries. The authors also noted learning disabilities in one-third of the cases.
quotes: Angle-closure glaucoma or occludable anterior chamber angles were present in three patients who were all older than 50 years of age and was treated by trabeculectomy, but the pathogenetic condition kept developing.
In the end, atrophia bulbi occurred in subjects III10 and III15 despite repeated surgeries (Table 1).
Learning disabilities were observed in one-third of the cases.

findings.statement: On histologic examination of sclera from affected members, Yu et al. (2009) found diffusely swollen collagen fibers that were twisted or frayed and mixed with normal fibers. In the 2 atrophied globes, collagen alignment was disrupted, the sclera contained coil-like amorphous material and was 3 times normal thickness, and the cornea was also thickened.
quotes: The diffusely swelled collagen fibers were twisted or frayed and were mixed with normal fibers (Figure 2A).

the alignment of collagen fibers was disrupted and there were a lot of coil-like amorphic materials in the scleras with three times the thickness of a normal sclera. The corneas were thickened as well.

findings.statement: In this Chinese family, Yu et al. (2009) found that the karyotype of all affected members was normal. Two-point linkage analysis with 23 microsatellite markers produced LOD scores below 1 for every marker, which excluded linkage to CHX10, PAX6, MFRP and to the loci on 14q32, 11p and 2q11-q14. The authors predicted that a novel locus was responsible.
quotes: Two-point LOD scores indicated that all 23 markers were less than 1 under different recombination fractions (Table 2).
we excluded the linkage of microphthalmia in this pedigree with the reported candidate genes (CHX10, PAX6, and MFRP) and loci (chromosomes 14q32, 11p, and 2q11-q14).
A novel locus is predicted to be responsible for the microphthalmia in this family.

findings.statement: Yu et al. (2009) concluded that excluding all known loci in this autosomal dominant family suggested high genetic heterogeneity in microphthalmia.
quotes: Microphthalmia has been mapped to different chromosomal regions, but this disease appears to be of high genetic heterogeneity, which was proven again in this study.
